pr_title: Poll all status data in Vera
pr_body:
Vera polling is not handled using hass event loops with proper backoffs.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Many people have reported that the vera component intermittently does not update some devices but eventually works after a few minutes. After reviewing the logs of several reporters, the best conclusion is that the vera controller does not always return accurate incremental status changes. This PR addresses the issue by requesting all the data and allowing HA decide what has changed. Additionally this PR also runs vera polling with HA event loops instead of a separate thread (which could have contributed to race conditions).

@vangorra I know you've been looking at how this works with different versions of HA and firmware. My vera is running quite old firmware (1.7.4000 - after a few broken upgrades I adapted an _upgrade when you have to_ approach with vera) and it hasn't changed for a long time.

My HA / vera setup had been very stable for a long time - and I hadn't updated my HA for a while either (0.103.6).

My HA config running on a mac was old (everything done in yaml files, lots of customisation, no use of the new guis) - and I was worried I was heading towards an unsupported setup - and I wasn't getting the benefits of all the great gui / config work - so I decided to build a new HA configuration from scratch using a Pi and the standard hassio build.

Anyhow vera is now working less well than it was - missing some updates etc. So I think that helps confirm :-

1. The problems are either something in HA or

@pavoni reported they are able to reproduce the issue and provided evidence suggesting that the controller is working normally. This isolates the original issue to a race condition caused by non thread safe code.
I update the PR to us long-polling (as it did before). This reduces polling to only as needed (around every 10 seconds) and provides near instant updates. Testers, please check the latest to confirm it works. I still cannot reproduce the issue.

I've updated two separate HA 111.1 systems with the latest code and so far I see no issues.   All Vera-created entities are showing their proper values when HA startup completes.

 Switching zwave devices on/off in the Vera web gui I can see the corresponding HA Lovelace switch toggle within a second or 2.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Using Vera temperature and humidity sensors there are random spikes in the values reported which are WAY out of the realms of sensibility. Temperature sensors that report values of +235C one moment and -17C the next. This is not limited to one sensor so it is not a single device fault. I've had temperatures of +3000C and 5000C reported - makes automations a bit tricky.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 110.2, 108.9
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): unsure
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: vera
- Link to integration documentation on our website: [(https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/vera)]
